Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell–cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

works.title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP-EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV-NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras-MAPK and PI3K-Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP-EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP-receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

works.title: Acute degradation of Pumilio proteins reveals a biphasic posttranscriptional regulatory hierarchy in embryonic stem cell fate decision
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Posttranscriptional regulation is critical for mammalian embryogenesis yet has been underexplored. We previously showed that RNA-binding Pumilio proteins (Pum1/2) are essential for early mouse embryogenesis and embryonic stem cell (ESC) functions. Here, using acute protein degradation systems combined with time-resolved RNA sequencing and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation, we delineate a two-phase regulatory hierarchy modulated by Pum1/2 in mouse ESCs. The first phase, occurring within 10 h of Pum1/2 depletion, is predominantly stabilization of over 100 Pum1/2-target mRNAs, while the second phase, occurring in subsequent 66 h, propagates to over 1,000 mRNAs mostly through indirect regulatory effects. Functionally, Pum1/2 depletion delays transition from naïve to formative pluripotency and alters expression trajectories of neuroectoderm and germline genes during early differentiation. Mechanistically, Pum1/2 directly repress mRNAs encoding Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 subunits, including Suz12 , thereby potentially constraining H3K27me3 deposition at neuroectodermal gene loci. These findings establish Pum1/2 as biphasic posttranscriptional regulators of pluripotency and lineage balance.

works.title: IFITM1-mediated restriction of henipavirus entry is associated with ephrinB2 reorganization and confinement in membrane nanodomains
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are prototype henipaviruses (HNV) within the family of Paramyxoviridae . They are highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxoviruses that cause fatal encephalitis in humans, with case fatality rates of 40 to 70%. These viruses use the receptor-binding protein (G) to engage host receptors ephrinB2 and/or ephrinB3, while the fusion protein (F) drives membrane fusion leading to virus entry and cell–cell fusion. Interferon-inducible transmembrane (IFITM) proteins restrict the infection of many unrelated viruses at virus entry. We show that the knockdown of IFITM1 enhances HNV entry and cell–cell fusion in both human epithelial and endothelial cells, while overexpression of IFITM1 inhibits both. Using single-molecule localization microscopy, we observed that IFITM1 forms nanoclusters on the plasma membrane that are enlarged upon interferon stimulation. IFITM1 clusters spatially co-occur with GM1-enriched, raft-like membrane domains. EphrinB2, a lipid raft resident, organizes into larger and denser clusters when associated with IFITM1, suggesting a preferential partitioning into membrane domains organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. Using single-particle tracking, we further show that lateral diffusion of ephrinB2 on the plasma membrane is confined in the presence of IFITM1. This confinement is not reversed by amphotericin B, nor is IFITM1-mediated NiV restriction. Our data show spatial reorganization and confinement of ephrinB2 within membrane domains that may be organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. These changes may contribute to HNV restriction, potentially by increasing the energy barrier for virus-cell membrane fusion and reducing productive virus-receptor encounters.

works.title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor-NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness-is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

works.title: Homeostatic control of stem cell activity during intestinal regeneration
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Stem cells proliferate rapidly to maintain tissue turnover during regeneration, yet the mechanisms preventing hyperproliferation remain unclear. Here, we identified nuclear factor Y (NF-Y) as a transcriptional repressor that maintains intestinal stem cell (ISC) quiescence. NF-Y restricts ISC proliferation by occupying the promoters of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling components, including Egfr , Mkp3 , Raf , Ras , and pnt , through regulation dependent on the histone acetyltransferase Nejire (Nej)/p300. Loss of NF-Y enhances ISC proliferation and accelerates tumor progression. NF-Y acts with Nej to restrict Egfr expression and suppress hyperproliferation. Together, these results demonstrate that NF-Y, acting with Nej, serves as a key transcriptional repressive brake that restrains growth-signaling to control stem cell activity under homeostatic and disease conditions.

works.title: VAMP725 and VAMP726 interact with cellulose synthase to support secondary cell wall formation
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: The formation of plant cell walls underpins morphogenesis, growth, and development of all plants. Cellulose is an essential and load-bearing cell wall polymer that is synthesized by Cellulose Synthase (CESA) protein complexes at the plasma membrane. In this study, we reveal that SNARE proteins Vesicle Associated Membrane Protein 726 (VAMP726) and VAMP725 associate with multiple CESA proteins. Consistent with these results, the VAMP726 is codelivered with the CESA proteins to the plasma membrane, and the proteins colocalize at intracellular compartments. We further show that the VAMPs, especially VAMP726, are important for CESA trafficking and sustenance of cellulose synthesis both in growing tissues and in secondary wall producing maturing tissues. Taken together, our study outlines an important intracellular process whereby VAMP proteins facilitate trafficking of CESA complexes during cellulose synthesis.

works.title: A trefoil knot mimic and multiple pore states define the mechanism of a split-shell Tc toxin
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Toxin complex (Tc) toxins are among the largest virulence factors secreted by pathogenic bacteria, operating via a sophisticated injection mechanism that translocates cytotoxic effectors into host cells. While most structural and mechanistic studies have focused on fused-shell Tc toxins such as PTC3 from Photorhabdus luminescens , the structurally distinct split-shell toxins remain poorly understood. Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the split-shell Yersinia entomophaga Tc holotoxin (YenTc) in multiple conformational states at resolutions of 2.6 to 3.7 Å. We show that the chitinase subunit YenChi2 is essential for shell expression and stabilizes the N terminus of the shell subunit YenA1 in the prepore state. Our structures also reveal the first trefoil knot mimic in Tc toxins, which serves the dual function of stabilizing the linker domain and holding the two halves of the split shell together. We further describe three distinct pore states: the conventional pore state, an inverted pore state in which the shell rotates 180° around a hinge in YenA2, and a lollipop pore state induced at alkaline pH in which the YenA1-YenChi2 subcomplex fully dissociates from the channel. Strikingly, all three pore states also manifest in the TcA pentamer of P. luminescens PTC3, indicating that they represent a general but previously undescribed feature of Tc toxin pore formation. Taken together, our results establish a mechanistic framework for split-shell Tc toxins and expose a dynamic, multilevel intoxication pathway that may apply broadly to Tc toxins.

works.title: Programmable multistable structures via bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Multistable structures, characterized by rapid shape morphing, instantaneous force amplification, and zero standby power, are pivotal for soft robotics and energy harvesting. However, achieving multistability while systematically controlling the accessible deformation modes remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing approach to design and fabricate programmable multistable structures, including octastable and various bistable units, mimicking the growth-induced morphing of plant leaves and fruits. The stability landscapes of these units can be tuned by varying dimensionless geometric parameters and validated through buckling analysis. By integrating multiple octastable units, we demonstrate a compact, 10-cm-scale strip and a shape-morphing metasurface with configuration spaces of over one billion and four sextillion stable states. Furthermore, by modulating the dimensionless geometric parameters of multiunit structures, we identify a transition from bending to folding, enabling the creation of bistable hinges. As proof-of-concept demonstrations, we developed devices for directional droplet routing and mixing, reconfigurable electrical switching, conforming grasping of irregular objects, and programmable mechanical display. This work establishes a versatile framework for the design and fabrication of next-generation reconfigurable morphing systems and programmable flexible devices.

works.title: Extracellular vesicles presenting “don’t eat me” signal limit the efferocytic capacity in lung fibrosis
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical "don't eat me" mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

works.title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8-DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s' C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8-Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8's ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock, upregulated HspA6 and HspA8 then limit the HSR presumably targeted by heat-induced DnaJB1. HspA6 knock-down and overproduction in HeLa cells suggest that HspA6 functions in preventing an overshoot of the HSR.

works.title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically nonperturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality , characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd 2 (Si 1− x Ge x ) 2 where, depending on x and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for x ≈ 0.1 by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

works.title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae , reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore–lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

works.title: Stereodynamical control of a four-atom reaction: HD + OH → D + H 2 O
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: To date, studies of differential steric effect in reactive collisions have been limited to atom + molecule systems. How stereodynamics is affected when the other reactant is also a molecule remains an open question. Here, we present a combined high-resolution crossed-beam scattering and full-dimensional quantum dynamical study of the HD ( v = 1, j = 2) + OH → D + H 2 O reaction, in which the HD molecular axis was initially prepared either parallel or perpendicular to the relative velocity using the stimulated Raman pumping scheme. The OH reactant was unpolarized and in its ground vibrational state, with a rotational temperature of ~85 K in the experiment, and was restricted to the ground rovibrational state in the theory. Pronounced stereodynamic effects are observed in both the backward scattering intensity and the product angular distributions. Detailed analysis of scattering wavefunctions reveals that the initial m = ±2 states access a noncoplanar dynamical transition state, distinct from that accessed by m = 0 ( m denotes the projection of j along the direction of relative velocity). The nonzero dihedral angle, a geometric degree of freedom absent in triatomic reactions, leads to reduced reactivity and enhances sideward scattering for the perpendicular configuration, while leaving the product rovibrational state distributions essentially unchanged. In addition, the alignment of the HD rotational angular momentum is preserved in the rotational direction of the product H 2 O.

works.title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
works.abstract: Abstract Tumour-promoting inflammation and immune evasion are key features of cancer, but prospective evidence linking specific immune pathways to prostate cancer risk remains limited. Here we show that circulating proteins involved in immune regulation may influence prostate cancer development. We analyse 368 immune- and inflammation-related proteins measured in blood samples from men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), including 1434 cases and matched controls, and combine these results with data from UK Biobank. While no proteins are associated with risk in EPIC alone after multiple testing correction, meta-analysis identifies several proteins linked to prostate cancer risk, including IL15 and FLT3LG, in particular, in blood taken long before diagnosis. Higher levels of immune surveillance-related proteins, particularly those involved in natural killer and T cell activity, are associated with lower prostate cancer risk, whereas genetic evidence implicates PARP1, SPINT2 and NME3 in increased risk. These findings suggest that immune pathways play a role in prostate cancer development and highlight potential targets for prevention.

works.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
works.abstract: Protists, defined as eukaryotes distinct from plants, animals and fungi, comprise much of eukaryotic phylogenetic diversity and perform key ecological functions, yet most lineages remain uncultivated and poorly represented in reference databases. Amplicon-based 18S rRNA gene surveys have transformed protist ecology, but primer bias, PCR bias and marker length can limit recovery of divergent lineages. Here, we conduct a cultivation-independent, rDNA operon-centered survey of over 30,000 assembled metagenomes, protist single-cell genomes and 21 long-amplicon datasets spanning marine, freshwater and soil-associated environments. We recover 157,956 long 18S rRNA gene sequences (≥800 bp), which together with reference sequences cluster into 103,338 OTUs at 97% identity and 24,438 OTUs at 85% identity. After excluding non-protist groups and singletons, 81% of the remaining 9543 protist 85%-OTUs consist exclusively of environmental sequences with no described representative. A concatenated 18S-28S rRNA framework reveals strong underrepresentation of Amoebozoa, Discoba, and Rhizaria in current references and identifies 13 candidate deeply divergent lineages with little or no database representation, some of which we link to partial genomes recovered by single-cell genomics. We further characterize their ecosystem distributions and predict associations with bacteria and other eukaryotes. This study provides a global, cultivation-independent resource for targeted sampling and downstream genomic, ecological and experimental characterization. In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

works.title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
works.abstract: Methane emissions account for nearly a third of the Earth’s effective radiative forcing, with methanotrophs playing a critical role in mitigating emissions by oxidising methane in diverse environments. Despite their ecological importance, methanotrophic diversity and environmental distribution remain incompletely characterised due to cultivation challenges, incomplete or low-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, and limited taxonomic resolution in marker gene surveys. Here, we present a national study of the biogeography of novel and known methanotrophs across Denmark’s major natural, urban and agricultural habitats, using genome-resolved classification of 10,683 metagenomes and 102 new methanotrophic species. By linking metabolic potential to habitat-specific distributions, we reveal uncharacterised methanotrophs as dominant in natural ecosystems. These findings provide a comprehensive baseline of methanotroph diversity, reveal clear contrasts between natural and disturbed habitats, and highlight candidate species and habitats for future methane-mitigation strategies. In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

works.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
works.abstract: Abstract Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry.

works.title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks
works.abstract: Flexible landing-pad sensor networks require local intelligence that can remain dormant for long periods yet respond rapidly to sparse mechanical events. General-purpose microcontrollers incur substantial retained-state and control overhead under such workloads, whereas hardwired controllers sacrifice programmability. Here we present Pico-X, a state-minimized eight-bit programmable processor designed for patch-level wake-up, sensing, event classification and reporting. A compact multi-cycle architecture, unified retentive memory and workload-constrained instruction framework reduce retained state and standby leakage. Fabricated in a 28-nanometre fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process, Pico-X consumes 728.2 nanowatts during active operation at 25 kilohertz and 24.9 nanowatts in state-retentive deep sleep without body bias, while preserving deterministic state recovery after wake-up. We further integrate Pico-X into a 4 × 4 flexible landing-pad demonstrator that records 12,842 events and achieves class-wise detection rates (recall) of 96.3% for occupancy, 92.1% for load imbalance, and 94.6% for deformation. Mean event-to-report latency is 38 milliseconds, packet delivery reaches 99.12%, and operation remains stable for more than 72 hours. These results establish a low-overhead programmable architecture for distributed, long-duration sensing. Researchers present Pico-X, a programmable microcontroller designed for sparse event-driven sensing. Operating at nanowatt power levels, it enables long-duration autonomous monitoring and reliable event detection in distributed flexible sensor networks.

works.title: Cryo-EM reveals conserved baseplate-architecture and distinct accessory-protein assemblies in mycobacteriophages Claus, Corndog and Mysterious
works.abstract: Mycobacteriophages, viruses infecting mycobacteria, hold therapeutic promise against antibiotic-resistant mycobacterial infections. Although thousands of mycobacteriophages have been isolated, high-resolution baseplate structures have been reported for only two, highlighting a gap in understanding phage–host interactions. Most mycobacteriophages are siphophages with four structural components: capsid, connector, non-contractile tail, and baseplate. The baseplate plays a critical role in host recognition, adsorption, and genome delivery. Here, we present atomic-resolution cryo-EM baseplate structures of three mycobacteriophages, Claus, Corndog, and Mysterious. These exhibit distinct inverted crown-, barrel-, and cage-like architectures, respectively, yet share a conserved architecture with a 6:6:3 stoichiometry of homohexameric tail tube proteins (TTPs), distal tail proteins (DTPs), and homotrimeric baseplate hub proteins (BHPs). The baseplate core is formed by DTPs and BHPs, with terminal TTPs making direct proximal contacts with DTPs and contributing to overall structure. While the central core is conserved, the exterior domains diverge across the phages. Surrounding the conserved cores are diverse baseplate accessory proteins (BAPs), including upper baseplate proteins (BppUs), central fiber proteins (CFPs), and others, which assemble into distinct peripheral architectures and give rise to two baseplate-opening mechanisms. These structures reveal a conserved baseplate core complex diversified by BAPs, a feature potentially shared across mycobacteriophage siphophage families. Atomic-resolution structures of three mycobacteriophages reveal a conserved baseplate core decorated by diverse accessory proteins, showing how related siphophages build distinct baseplate architectures from a common structural core.

works.title: Electric vehicle battery materials supply disruptions can be mitigated with chemistry changes and recycling
works.abstract: Battery materials supply chains for plug-in electric vehicles face vulnerabilities to disruptions from geopolitical disputes and natural disasters. Through industry interviews, we identify scenarios that could disrupt materials supply by 2030. We estimate the impacts on US automotive production, prices, and consumer costs in an economic equilibrium model of the US automotive industry. We find year-long disruptions can have large impacts: trade restrictions that reduce processed lithium supply from China by 30% and disasters shutting down the three largest cobalt mines increase average new vehicle prices (including conventional vehicles and plug-in electric vehicles) by $1,100-1,600, costing consumers $14-17 billion. However, feasible changes in battery chemistry and materials supply by 2030 mitigate these negative impacts. If 85% of battery electric vehicle models are produced with lithium iron phosphate batteries and at least 100 kilotonnes of planned production of recycled lithium carbonate equivalent is available, disruption costs decrease by more than half. This study shows that disruptions in US battery materials supply could cost tens of billions of dollars. However, feasible changes in battery chemistry and increasing recycled lithium supply largely reduce the consequences of the disruptions.

works.title: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes and mapping of host and bacteria remodelling of the intracellular niche
works.abstract: Macrophages engulf pathogens into dynamic phagosomes, which many bacteria manipulate for survival. However, isolating pure pathogen-containing phagosomes remains challenging. Here, we developed a novel flow cytometry-based isolation and ultrasensitive proteomics approach to analyse phagosomal and bacterial proteomes from macrophages infected with wild-type (WT) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STM) or a ΔphoP mutant at 30 min and 4 hours post-infection. Our approach provides higher throughput, requires lower cell numbers and quantifies more proteins than previous techniques. Our data reveals key host-pathogen interactions, showing induction of PhoP-dependent virulence factors and novel putative proteins that shape STM's intracellular niche. Moreover, our data indicates that bacteria-containing phagosomes recruit mitochondrial membrane for production of reactive oxygen species. These findings provide new insights into Salmonella's manipulation of phagosomal maturation and intracellular niche formation.

works.title: Vertebrate paired fins are specified by an ancient dorso-ventral patterning system
works.abstract: The origin of paired fins was a major event in early vertebrate history that fueled the adaptive radiation of the gnathostome clade. Evidence for the conservation of ancient regulatory systems between paired and median fins supports a model in which appendage-patterning mechanisms first evolved in the midline and were later redeployed to a new embryonic context, the flank. However, while paired fins and limbs are asymmetric along the dorsoventral (DV) axis, the equivalent axis does not exist in median fins, which are symmetric across the midline, raising questions of how DV patterning evolved. Here, we combine genetic tools in zebrafish with comparative expression analyses in representative ray-finned and cartilaginous fishes to show that a subset of limb DV patterning genes are expressed during median fin development. Using genetic lineage tracing of the canonical limb dorsalizing factor lmx1bb , we further demonstrate that, although lmx1bb -derived cells occupy distinct spatial domains across fin types, a subset of this lineage is fated to differentiate into fin ray osteoblasts in both paired and median fins. To test the potential conservation of regulatory modules across fin types, we generated a series of deletion mutants for two known lmx1b mouse limb enhancers, LARM1 and LARM2, that we show are partially conserved upstream of zebrafish lmx1bb . These experiments revealed that LARM function is essential for dorsoventral patterning of the paired pectoral and pelvic fins of zebrafish but is dispensable for formation of the unpaired dorsal and anal fins. Collectively, these data support the conservation of an ancient LARM -Lmx1b dorsal determination system in the paired fins of osteichthyans, challenge models proposing simple co-option of a pre-existing median fin gene regulatory network and suggest that the acquisition of this regulatory module may have been a key early step in the evolution of the paired fin DV patterning axis.

works.title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce SCIMUSE , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94 σ ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale interdisciplinary expert evaluation, paving the way to study and improve difficult-to-measure metrics such as expert-perceived scientific interestingness.

works.title: Coevolution of social network structure and life history in toothed whales
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Toothed whales offer a 34 My-long natural experiment for the evolution of complex mammalian societies. However, quantitative comparative analyses of social structure in these species are lacking. Here, we draw on existing social network analyses to compare social structure across toothed whales. We consider published measures of two social network traits across all toothed whales: modularity ([Formula: see text]), which captures divisions or "cliques" in a social community, and social differentiation ([Formula: see text]), which estimates how much whales vary in their relationships-whether they associate equally with others or form special bonds with specific individuals. Combining these with a recently published database of life history traits, we applied phylogenetic multilevel models with the objective of exploring the origins of social network structure. We identified 98 measures of modularity and 89 measures of social differentiation from 23 toothed whale species. Social network structure was more similar among closely related species (showing strong phylogenetic signal), despite substantial intraspecific variability. Toothed whales with longer lifespans and larger bodies tended to form more modular social networks, as did those where males were proportionally larger than females. Similar but weaker patterns were found between life history traits and social differentiation. Results from causal coevolutionary models provide preliminary evidence that social structure has been both a leader and follower of changes in life history. Our findings reveal the correlated evolution of social network structure and life history traits in toothed whales, shedding new light on the origins of social relationships.

works.title: Signaling mechanism of the transmembrane energy receptor Aer
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: The Escherichia coli aerotaxis receptor Aer is a bacterial chemoreceptor that senses intracellular redox changes via an N-terminal PAS domain bound to a flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) cofactor. Distinct from canonical methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs) such as Tar/Tsr, Aer lacks a periplasmic ligand-binding domain and adaptive methylation, transmitting conformational signals laterally from the PAS domain to the HAMP domain and the methylation helix-like cap (MHL-cap) of the kinase control domain (KCD). To elucidate the Aer signaling mechanism, we determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of full-length Aer in oxidized flavin quinone (kinase-on) and reduced semiquinone (kinase-off) states. Structural comparison reveals redox-linked rearrangements of the FAD-binding pocket, reorientation of PAS–HAMP interactions, and strikingly altered MHL-cap stability. PAS–MHL-cap interactions in the oxidized state compress the receptor and stabilize the proximal KCD helices, whereas reduction disrupts these contacts, increasing KCD flexibility. To probe distal effects on KCD architecture, we performed nanodisc reconstitution and pulse dipolar ESR spectroscopy on spin-labeled positions along the four-helix bundle. Distance distributions indicate redox-dependent changes in helix separation, particularly at the C-terminal MHL2 region, consistent with PAS-driven loosening of KCD packing in kinase-off states. These data support a model in which FAD redox chemistry reorganizes flavin pocket residues that in turn subtly alter PAS conformation to influence PAS–HAMP and PAS–MHL-cap packing and hence KCD conformational stability. The findings reveal an Aer-specific signaling axis distinct from periplasmic-ligand binding MCPs that has adapted MCP architecture for lateral PAS input and cytoplasmic redox sensing.

works.title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: As deep learning for physical systems continues to grow in popularity, efforts to improve generalizability have primarily focused on designing architectures that embed physical constraints. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Here, we examine whether training datasets themselves can be optimized to improve generalization. We introduce a method to create datasets that produce emulators capable of generalizing to new, structurally different scenarios absent from the training data. We use a differentiable simple climate model (SCM) to calculate the sensitivity of emulator loss to perturbations in the training data, iteratively updating the training data to maximize emulator skill. For an SCM, an emulator trained on one scenario optimized in this fashion outperforms an emulator trained on six standard Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) pathways. We achieve this higher predictive skill despite training on a smaller dataset, finding that our emulator successfully isolates distinct physical behaviors of different climate forcing agents (e.g., greenhouse gases vs. aerosols) without single-forcing runs. We then demonstrate that scenarios optimized using an SCM, when used to drive an intermediate-complexity climate model, produce a training dataset that yields a more skillful emulator than training on ScenarioMIP outputs. Our results suggest that, in the compute-constrained environment of running full-scale climate models, generating a small number of dynamically rich scenarios provides greater marginal value for emulation and characterizing system responses than expanding the suite of traditional emissions pathways.

works.title: Millennial-scale variability in Greenland dust provenance during Dansgaard–Oeschger events of the last glacial period
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Greenland ice-core records show an approximately 15-fold increase in dust concentration during cold stadial periods compared to warmer interstadial periods in the last glacial period (LGP). While multiple regions including East Asian deserts and the Sahara have been suggested as potential source areas (PSAs) for Greenland dust, millennial-scale variability of their relative contributions associated with Dansgaard-Oeschger climatic fluctuations during the LGP remains poorly constrained. To address this, we investigate high-resolution (~800 y) Pb and Sr isotopic, mineralogical, and geochemical records from the North Greenland Eemian Ice Drilling ice-core samples covering the entire LGP. We found that the Pb and Sr isotopic compositions, kaolinite-to-chlorite ratios, and chemical index of alteration values were higher during stadials than during interstadials. Comparison with PSAs suggests that East Asian deserts remained the dominant contributors to Greenland dust throughout the LGP, but contributions from the Sahara increased during stadial intervals. This shift likely reflects climate-driven changes in atmospheric circulation patterns responsible for transporting dust to Greenland. Our findings provide insights into the relationship between dust cycle dynamics and abrupt climate changes on millennial timescales during the LGP.

works.title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion
works.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

works.title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
works.abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth's core. Here we use a new high-pressure method - microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells - to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 [Formula: see text] cm measurement of liquid iron's resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today's lowermost mantle is fully solid.

works.title: Dual-acting compounds that deliver an acidifying domain via zanamivir to the virus surface are potent influenza inhibitors
works.abstract: While contemporary antiviral development primarily strives to produce “lock and key” inhibitors, we present here a different approach to drug design that uses compounds devised to alter the microenvironment of the virion surface, making it incompatible with virus entry. We illustrate this strategy with inhibitors of influenza virus and show that compounds designed to produce a proton-rich mantle above the virion surface affect the ability of the viral hemagglutinin to interact with cellular receptors and gain entry to the cell. The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in ferrets and in mice after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically.

works.title: Identification of a specialized lipid barrier for Drosophila metamorphosis
works.abstract: Many terrestrial insects transition from humid to dry environments at metamorphosis, yet how they avoid dehydration is unclear. In Drosophila melanogaster , we identify a lipid barrier to water loss in the pupa that is anatomically distinct from that of the adult. It comprises unisex hydrocarbons that are longer and less volatile than their sex-specific adult counterparts. These hyperlong hydrocarbons are produced by larval oenocytes and stored in the fat body for subsequent transport to the cuticle at pupariation. A fatty acid elongase, EloHL, is required for hyperlong hydrocarbon biosynthesis and for a functional barrier to dehydration during early metamorphosis. Hyperlong barrier hydrocarbons are widespread across the Drosophila genus and typically transition to shorter sex-specific versions during adult maturation. In the desert species D. mojavensis , however, adults retain hyperlong hydrocarbons. This study reveals how insect lipid barriers are tuned to environmental variations in aridity and temperature during development and evolution.

works.title: Pink noise in dyads’ semantic similarity trajectories predicts conversation enjoyment
works.abstract: Conversation is a core component of human social life. Many influential theories treat conversation as a linear system, i.e., the sum of its parts. However, linear accounts of semantic entrainment lose explanatory power at their upper limits: Discussing perfectly aligned opinions becomes boring. We propose an alternate account that considers the multiscale organization of semantic similarity over the course of a conversation, as indexed by pink noise. Here, we test whether pink noise can be found in interlocutors' conavigated trajectories through semantic space. Not only is pink noise present, but its strength predicts positive conversation outcomes like enjoyment and connection, increases with practice, and is reflected in a large language model's representation of conversation quality. These results demonstrate an important role for scale-free dynamics in characterizing successful conversation.

works.title: Spatial proteomics reveals lipid droplet reorganization in symbiotic Paramecium bursaria cells
works.abstract: Endosymbiosis is an important adaptive mechanism allowing organisms to exploit previously inaccessible niches. The flexible relationship between the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and green algae represents a model system for studying early endosymbiosis evolution. However, the mechanisms underlying how P. bursaria cells maintain this endosymbiotic relationship remain unclear. Here, we use mass spectrometry–based proteomics to generate a spatial proteomic atlas of the host P. bursaria cells with and without endosymbionts. This atlas defines the protein composition of the endosymbiont-containing compartment (perialgal vacuole) and reveals pronounced remodeling of host lipid droplets upon symbiosis. Imaging analyses confirm that lipid droplets change in size, morphology, and positioning, accumulating near intracellular algae. Perturbing symbiotic cells with chemical inhibitors of lipid metabolism reduces endosymbiotic algal numbers, revealing a role for lipid droplets in the host-endosymbiont interaction. Our data provide a comprehensive resource for protein localization in P. bursaria cells and elucidate how those cells remodel an existing cellular compartment to maintain endosymbiosis.

works.title: Comprehensive degron mapping in human transcription factors
works.abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. Active degrons placed within exposed and intrinsically disordered regions contribute to modulating the abundance of the transcription factors, while the most common somatic mutations that are linked to skin cutaneous melanoma lead to unfolding and exposure of a latent degron buried in the zinc finger structure. We present examples of compartment-specific degrons and demonstrate that variant effects in transcription factors correlate with degron potency. Last, we show that while >60% of all predicted transcriptional activation domains overlap with strong degrons, acidic residues within the remaining transactivating regions counter the degron potency, showing how degrons can shape the transcription factor sequence landscape.

works.title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
works.abstract: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical processes. Here, we use an explainable machine-learning framework to investigate interactions among atmospheric circulation, surface soil moisture, and temperature, and their role in recent heat extremes. We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, ∼10% to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across ∼28% of humid mid-latitude regions. We further reveal that this interaction is systematically underestimated in CMIP6 and CESM2 Large Ensemble simulations. Soils in climate models are too dry at the initiation of heat waves, therefore suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation. These findings help explain regional model biases in upper-tail warming and highlight avenues for improving future projections of extreme heat events.

works.title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
works.abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a powerful and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow-noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 kelvin. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 megahertz (138 million revolutions per minute) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate of 4.75 × 10 −7 hertz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Last, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a previously unidentified regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.

works.title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
works.abstract: Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5° to 2°C require rapid emission reductions alongside additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ∼2 to 3 PgC year −1 . Our simulations show that sustained century-scale ocean iron fertilization (OIF) in the southern sector of the Southern Ocean (SSO) provides a contribution of ∼30 PgC, equivalent to ∼0.3 PgC year −1 . This uptake nearly matches the additional carbon uptake from global fertilization. In other iron-limited regions, fertilization-induced uptake is largely offset (70 to 100%) by anomalous outgassing in nonfertilized regions. After terminating OIF following 30 years of fertilization, the ocean retains ∼50% of the additional carbon in the SSO, whereas retention is negligible elsewhere. These results identify the SSO as the most favorable region for durable carbon removal through large-scale OIF, particularly in terms of additionality and durability, although its carbon uptake is smaller than earlier estimates. OIF-induced CDR is constrained by local and remote nutrient depletion, carbon reentrainment, incomplete macronutrient drawdown, and reduced phytoplankton carbon-to-phosphorus ratios. Incomplete macronutrient drawdown reflects the uptake controls by light, top-down controls, and rates of macronutrient resupply. Further insight into OIF potential will be enabled by standardized multimodel comparisons and targeted analysis of nutrient drawdown controls.

works.title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection
works.abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

works.title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca2+ oscillations and fertility in mice
works.abstract: Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca2+) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. However, whether PLCζ1 alone accounts for Ca2+ release at fertilization in all mammals remains uncertain. Male mice lacking Plcζ1 exhibit subfertility and reduced litter sizes; their sperm induce delayed, low-frequency Ca2+ oscillations, indicating a compensatory mechanism. Notably, mouse sperm express high levels of PLCδ4, essential for completing the acrosome reaction (AR). In Plcζ1-null sperm, PLCδ4 is upregulated and retained post-AR. These observations suggest a secondary functional role for PLCδ4. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated Plcδ4 knockout (KO) mice. Plcδ4-null sperm trigger attenuated, delayed Ca2+ oscillations and significantly reduced fertilization rates, indicating that PLCδ4 contributes to but does not independently drive Ca2+ signaling. We therefore generated a Double Knockout (DKO) mouse line lacking both sperm-enriched PLCs. DKO males were sterile, with sperm failing to induce Ca2+ oscillations, and the isolated residual Ca2+ rise was insufficient to activate eggs. These findings reveal that PLCζ1, the primary oscillator, and PLCδ4, a compensatory factor, work cooperatively within a complex, multi-component PLC system that ensures robust fertilization. This work reveals molecular specialization among mammals in initiating the fertilization Ca2+ signals. It has implications for understanding male infertility, improving assisted reproductive technologies, and developing contraceptive strategies.

works.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
works.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

works.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
works.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

works.title: Can the exposome help solve the alcohol and cancer mystery?
works.abstract: Alcohol consumption is a preventable driver of many cancers, yet a central biological question remains unresolved: by what mechanisms does ethanol promote malignancy? We propose that alcohol in the context of the exposome (i.e., the network of chemical, biological, and social determinants that interact with ethanol across the life span) provides a unifying framework for understanding alcohol-related carcinogenesis. Viewed through the lens of the exposome, alcohol is not only as a direct carcinogen but also as a systemic amplifier of environmental risk acting across multiple levels of biological organization, from molecular damage to whole-body physiology. This reframing has important implications for mechanistic research, precision prevention, and public-health policy.

works.title: Two parallel lateral hypothalamic GABAergic projections differentially modulate pain and anxiety in mice
works.abstract: The lateral hypothalamus (LH) is fundamentally involved in motivated behaviors, yet the precise functional segregation of its GABAergic projections in modulating pain and its affective dimensions remains poorly understood. Here, using male and female mice, we revealed that LH GABAergic neurons sent parallel projections to two pivotal pain and affect processing centers: the lateral parabrachial nucleus (LPB) and the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT). In vivo fiber photometry revealed that LH GABAergic terminals in both the PVT and LPB are robustly activated by noxious, aversive, and rewarding stimuli, indicating their roles in encoding salient and affective information. Critically, we uncovered a remarkable functional segregation of these LH GABAergic pathways. Optogenetic activation of the LH-PVT projection exerted anxiogenic effects without altering pain sensitivity in both naïve and neuropathic pain mice; whereas optogenetic inhibition of this pathway exerted significant analgesic and anxiolytic effects specifically in neuropathic pain, highlighting a context-dependent modulation of pain and affect. In contrast, optogenetic activation of the LH-LPB projection induced contralateral pronociception without impacting affective behaviors, conversely, inhibition of this pathway significantly elevated contralateral pain thresholds in both physiological and neuropathic pain conditions. We also demonstrated that stimulation of the LH-LPB projection acted via a disinhibitory mechanism involving local LPB GABAergic interneurons to enhance activity of LPB glutamatergic neurons. Collectively, our findings delineate two parallel and functionally segregated LH GABAergic output pathways that differentially control distinct aspects of pain experience, thereby offering novel circuit-specific targets for the treatment of chronic pain and its debilitating emotional comorbidities.
